brand.name: Break Free
brand.tagline: you say who does the work; it gets carried out, checked, and followed through

videos.title: What Break Free actually does
videos.subtitle: you say who does the work; it gets carried out and checked

lines.text: You are in your coding agent, and you already know what you want done and who should do it.
Saying it is easy. Carrying it out is not, and knowing it was actually checked is harder still.
Break Free takes the instruction you would give anyway. Use this for that.
Name a model, like DeepSeek or a local Ollama, and it runs as a delegated worker.
Name another harness, like Codex or omp, and it opens there in a terminal session, on your subscription.
You also say how it gets checked, and the gateway runs that command itself after the worker finishes.
Anything you started stays open until it is resolved, so a failed run is not quietly left behind.
You stay the one deciding. Break Free carries it out, and proves it.

videos.title: Hand a task to another model
videos.subtitle: name the model, name the check

chapters.heading: Hand a task to another model

lines.text: The task: unit tests for the router. Worth doing well, not worth your most expensive model.
So you say it plainly. Use DeepSeek to write them, and check them with npm test.
DeepSeek is a model, so it is delegated, with permission to read, write and run, and nothing else.
The gateway runs the tests itself, and you get a diff that already passed, naming the model that wrote it.

videos.title: Send work to another harness
videos.subtitle: Codex, omp or pi, on your subscription

lines.text: The task: something you would rather Codex did, with its own memory, skills and tools.
You say: use Codex for this one.
Codex is a harness, not a model, so it opens in a real terminal session inside your repository.
It runs on your subscription. Attach to watch it, or leave it working and read it back later.

videos.title: Split one job across several
videos.subtitle: in parallel, with the checks you named

lines.text: The task: rate limiting. Really four pieces of work, and they do not all need the same model.
You say who does what, and what depends on what.
The core goes first. The moment its check passes, the rest start together on the models you named.
A failed check stops that branch, and one report comes back with every result attached.

videos.title: Get an independent verdict
videos.subtitle: from a vendor that did not write it

lines.text: The task: this is about to land, and you want it read by something that did not write it.
You say: have Kimi review it. The real diff goes to a different vendor.
Back comes approve, revise or reject, with a file and a line for each issue. You still decide.

videos.title: Nothing gets left behind
videos.subtitle: the turn will not end on a failed run

lines.text: The work is done and pushed. This is the moment things usually get forgotten.
The push records the run it just caused, and a watcher resolves it by asking GitHub, not by asking a model.
The run fails. That failure is now open work, carrying the job that broke and a link to it.
So the turn refuses to end. You are told, before anyone walks away from it.

videos.title: Pick up where you left off
videos.subtitle: the log lives in the repository

chapters.heading: Pick up where you left off

lines.text: Context windows end. Projects do not.
Every task, decision and gotcha was written to plain Markdown inside your repository as it happened.
You ask to resume, and it tells you what is in progress, what is blocked, and what is ready.
